clue.text: Large rat goes around, one providing diversion

indicators.note: the rat goes around the other piece, so that piece sits inside it

parts.note: a rat is a turncoat who deserts his side
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big rodent scurrying in circles to create a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFECTOR wraps around L to give DEFLECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A deflector is a device or person that turns something aside, so it provides a diversion.

clue.text: Swim with hot swimwear in sound

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
H for hot, as on a tap
a skimpy style of bathing costume

explanation.surface: Going for a swim on a hot day in a skimpy costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A diphthong is a vowel sound that glides from one quality to another within a syllable.

clue.text: Those who execute reverse if bike follows circles

indicators.note: the bike comes after the circles, fixing the order of the last two pieces
the instruction to reverse turns the little word that follows it back to front

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about pedalling in circles, framed by a grim group of executioners.
explanation.walkthrough: FI + RINGS + QUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A firing squad is the group of soldiers detailed to shoot a condemned prisoner, carrying out the death sentence.

clue.text: Bill wearing woman's skirt

indicators.note: the woman wears the bill, so it ends up inside her name

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill

explanation.surface: A man called Bill dressed in a woman's skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like the garment Bill is wearing, but it is a verb meaning dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to go round it without tackling it, which is to evade it.

clue.text: Frenzied rite thus engulfs ill-omened figure

indicators.note: engulfs means the first word swallows the rearranged letters

parts.note: then can mean thus, as in therefore

indicators.note: frenzied signals the letters are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A frantic ritual takes over, with an unlucky number in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the number traditionally thought unlucky, so it is an ill-omened figure.

clue.text: After service lift provided by a basket-maker?

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the armed service, setting the order

parts.note: the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word raises it from bottom to top, so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: After church, a lift home offered by a weaver of baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF + FI + A. The question mark flags that the definition names a material that makes baskets, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm-leaf fibre woven into baskets and mats, so it is something that makes a basket.

clue.text: Publisher rebuffed piece of writing that's rot

indicators.note: something rebuffed is pushed back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, the person who puts a publication out
an essay or other written work

explanation.surface: An author's work turned away by a publisher as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: DE + COMPOSITION. 'Rot' poses as a dismissive verdict on the writing, but it is the noun for decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is the process of decay, and decomposition is the breaking down of organic matter.

clue.text: Being untrue is dashed silly today

indicators.note: dashed means smashed to pieces, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that infidelity is a foolish modern habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being untrue to a friend or cause is faithlessness, which is what disloyalty is.

clue.text: Something indicating Kiss title track is running

parts.note: an X, a cross, marks a kiss in a letter
a count is a nobleman's title
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A song called Kiss is now playing as a track title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss' and 'track' look like a band and a song; Kiss is the X at the end of a letter, and track is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-country is a kind of running over open fields and hills rather than on a track.

clue.text: White part of gazelle, somewhat towards the top

indicators.note: in a down entry, going towards the top means the letters run upwards
only a portion of the following words is wanted, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A white patch on a gazelle sits up near the top of its body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like the colour of the gazelle's markings; it is a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the Mosel valley in Germany, so a white in wine-list shorthand.

clue.text: Unsophisticated trash is in no lemonade

indicators.note: to trash something is to wreck it, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is no rubbish in the lemonade, from someone naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one-dimensional lacks depth or complexity, so it is simplistic and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Like some rulers dismissing a risk

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: Emperors who shrug off any danger.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPERIAL without its A. 'Rulers' could also be measuring sticks marked in imperial units.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it in danger, which is to risk it.

clue.text: Counterpart right to block popular tune that's mistimed

indicators.note: something that blocks a passage sits in the middle of it

parts.note: oppo is British slang for one's opposite number

explanation.surface: A rival's work interrupts a hit song at the wrong moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppo is British slang for a colleague or opposite number; 'popular' gives the in of 'in fashion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inopportune happens at an unsuitable or awkward moment, so it is badly timed.

clue.text: Mark in college raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: A grade awarded at a school that has been pushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a written mark or annotation, and one can note or mark something down.

clue.text: As some say, Dorothy or Charlie's coat

indicators.note: what some people say is spoken, so a word is matched by its sound

parts.note: the surname shared by the writer Dorothy and the jazzman Charlie, said with a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Wondering which of two famous people owns this jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy Parker was a witty American writer and Charlie Parker a jazz saxophonist; in a non-rhotic accent the surname matches the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, so a kind of outer coat.

clue.text: One's repeated no fun getting drunk — as these are

definitions.text: One's repeated no fun getting drunk — as these are

indicators.note: getting drunk suggests a tipsy stagger, so the letters are scrambled
repeated means the pair for one's is written down twice

parts.note: one is I and 's stands for is, giving I then S

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that being drunk is no fun, as these drinks are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' gives ISIS from 'One's' (I plus 's as IS); 'getting drunk' rearranges that with NO and FUN. The whole clue works as the definition too: teas and tisanes are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal teas made by steeping leaves are sipped, often as a sober alternative, hence 'no fun getting drunk'.

clue.text: Retired flier delaying one achievement

parts.note: an ex- holder of a post has retired from it

indicators.note: delaying the one makes it turn up later in the word, dropped in further along

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former airman held back from one great deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The one is not added but moved: it is taken out of the retired flier and dropped back in two letters later.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring deed, and so an achievement worth recounting.

clue.text: Rascal adapts ancient game without hesitation in book

parts.note: a tinker is a mischievous child
to tailor something is to adapt it

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the game wraps round the hesitation

parts.note: I spy, the children's guessing game

explanation.surface: A naughty child changing the rules of an old game smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'minus', but here it is the old sense, outside. I spy is a children's guessing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy is John le Carré's 1974 spy novel featuring George Smiley.

clue.text: Guide Europeans over pitch

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece over another is written above it

parts.note: pitch is a black tar-like substance

explanation.surface: Someone showing European visitors round a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a playing field; it is the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole star stays almost fixed above the north pole, so sailors used it to guide navigation.

clue.text: Cricket side with test location for players

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, used here of where actors appear

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
to screen a patient is to test them

explanation.surface: A cricket team and a Test match ground, where the players are.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side. The players are actors, not cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors in film or television perform on-screen, so it is the place where those players appear.

clue.text: Retailer, quiet about poor line, is to stock up again

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the reworked letters

parts.note: a rep, or sales representative, is a seller of goods
sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: poor signals the word is badly formed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says little about a weak product line and is restocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill up again, which is restocking supplies.

clue.text: Worry about old figure producing plant hydrocarbon

indicators.note: the worry goes about the rest, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Fretting over an ancient number that yields a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotene is the orange pigment in carrots, a hydrocarbon made by plants.

clue.text: Deliberately hands round a board game

indicators.note: the two hands go round the next word, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Someone passing round a board game on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberately' looks like an adverb about the handing round; it is the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction to play slowly and broadly, so deliberately in tempo.

clue.text: Family member left complaint involving attacks

explanation.surface: A relative went away with an illness that brings fits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, as in departed; it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand mal is a severe form of epilepsy, a disorder involving seizures, which are attacks.

clue.text: Seat in empty gallery likely to snap?

indicators.note: the seat goes in the emptied word, inside its shell
emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A chair in a deserted gallery that might break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like furniture; it is the backside. A grumpy person snaps at people.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy person is bad-tempered and liable to snap irritably at others, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One's charged for not retreating

definitions.note: read as 'one is charged', describing the answer

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone facing a charge for refusing to back down.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO + TON. 'Charged' suggests an accused person; it means carrying electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a subatomic particle carrying a positive electric charge.

clue.text: Dog circles stallion dropping head in fatigue

indicators.note: the dog circles the horse, enclosing it

parts.note: the famous collie of film and television

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a stud is a stallion kept for breeding

explanation.surface: A dog circling a weary horse that hangs its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the collie of the films; a stud is a breeding stallion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental weariness, a lack of energy, so fatigue.

clue.text: Garments of swimmer on lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another is placed above it

parts.note: Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Clothing belonging to someone swimming in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like a person; in crosswords it is often a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes, a class of intimate clothing.

clue.text: Accusing Punjabi's group can end in snag

parts.note: Indic is the branch of languages that includes Punjabi

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A band from the Punjab facing a hitch at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict someone is to formally charge them with a crime, so accusing them.

clue.text: One predicting development of giant root crops

indicators.note: development changes a thing into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A forecaster who predicts the growth of enormous vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosticator forecasts future events, so is someone who predicts.

clue.text: What distracts ruddy husband, misbehaving

explanation.surface: A flushed husband behaving badly makes a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue that draws attention away from the real issue.

clue.text: Look around in theatre, place for acting

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, inside it

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: turned around means read backwards

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: Glancing about a theatre for a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rep is short for repertory theatre, a company staging a rotating set of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Role-play is acting out a part, as in training exercises or therapy.

clue.text: Nation's first person sought office

explanation.surface: A country's first leader stood for election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' looks like a founding leader; it is the pronoun I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, so a nation.

clue.text: Scrap books with divine pieces inside

indicators.note: inside means these pieces go within the books letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine or clergyman
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper tucked into religious books.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover bit or remnant, so a scrap.

clue.text: Plant extract which art collector has to have?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aromatic oil distilled from a plant

definitions.text: which art collector has to have?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: an oil painting that a collector cannot do without

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads 'essential' as must-have and 'oil' as an oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential oil is a concentrated volatile oil taken from a plant, used in perfume and aromatherapy.

clue.text: Conservative admitted to fondness for defeat

indicators.note: admitted to a place means let inside it

explanation.surface: A Tory confesses to a soft spot for losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitted' looks like confessed; it means let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A licking is informal for a heavy beating or decisive defeat.

clue.text: Make firm study works for one partner

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
pieces of music for one performer
a date is the person one goes out with

explanation.surface: Analysing which business tasks suit one partner.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLI is the plural of solo, a piece for a single performer.
explanation.definitionFit: To consolidate is to strengthen and make more solid or secure.

clue.text: In the auditorium, didn't catch film

indicators.note: an auditorium is where people listen, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer in the theatre missed the movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; it is a thin layer or haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a thin coating or haze, as of moisture on glass, which a mist is.

clue.text: Litter in saloon for American President

parts.note: Americans call a saloon car a sedan
the chair presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: Rubbish found in an American president's car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish; it is an old word for a covered seat carried on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a carried couch or chair, and a sedan chair is an enclosed seat borne by two porters.

clue.text: A rebel here in France engaged by servant for painter

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in 1450

indicators.note: engaged by someone means taken on and held within their service

explanation.surface: A revolutionary in France is hired by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450. A painter elected to the Royal Academy is an Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: An academician is a member of an academy of art, such as a Royal Academician, often a painter.

clue.text: More confused with metric gauge

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: Someone even more muddled by metric measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A micrometer is a precision instrument for measuring very small thicknesses, so a kind of measuring gauge.

clue.text: Two strikes, one pushing back litres in kitchen vessel

indicators.note: the second strike shoves its letter for litres further back

parts.note: a punch and a blow are two strikes

explanation.surface: A kitchen brawl in which someone sends a bowl of liquid flying.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOW has its L pushed to the end to make BOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch bowl is a large bowl for serving punch, a mixed drink.

clue.text: Extract from Biblical figure quoted

parts.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel
cit. is the abbreviation for cited

explanation.surface: A passage taken from the words of a Bible character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like a noun for a quoted passage; it is the verb draw out.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it out of someone, so to extract it.

clue.text: Bug spies used to trap villain

indicators.note: a trap holds its prey inside it

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Secret agents plant a listening device to catch a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' and 'spies' suggest surveillance; the bug is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a true bug, an insect of the order Hemiptera known for its loud song.

clue.text: Old lady overwhelmed by change, being old school

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed and swallowed up inside

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman swamped by change at her former school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is the school or university one used to attend.

clue.text: Force Cicero to wriggle about

indicators.note: to wriggle means the letters of the Roman's name twist into a new order

explanation.surface: Pressure on the Roman orator to squirm out of an awkward position.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion is persuading by threats or force, so the noun force fits.

clue.text: Oscar, in trouble, beginning to imbibe the sauce

indicators.note: Oscar goes in the trouble, inside it

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Oscar, in a bad way, has started on the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sauce' looks like alcohol, which Oscar takes to; it is a garlic sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal garlic mayonnaise, a cold sauce.

clue.text: Dislike current lines by bard

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone disapproving of up-to-date verses by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dislike' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or animosity towards someone, so a feeling of dislike.

clue.text: Understood piece of pottery is reserved

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said

explanation.surface: A pot that has been set aside, by unspoken agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' suggests a booked item; it means quiet and withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little and keeps to themselves, so is reserved in manner.

clue.text: Bends stick broken by Roman here

indicators.note: a stick broken by something has that thing driven into its middle

explanation.surface: A Roman snapping a walking stick that bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bends' looks like a verb about the stick; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicane is a sharp S-bend inserted in a racing circuit to slow the cars.

clue.text: Enduring wish to be given name

parts.note: to long for is to wish for
a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: Hoping to be given a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term means lasting for an extended period, so enduring rather than brief.

clue.text: When climbing, wears bits of leather

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: A rock climber's gear made of leather.
explanation.walkthrough: SPORTS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Strops are leather straps, used for sharpening razors.

clue.text: Kind of speech by one still defending unusually realist aim, in theory

parts.note: a dialect is a regional variety of speech
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: defending means guarding, so the still word wraps round the next piece
unusually means out of the ordinary way, so realist aim is rearranged

explanation.surface: A pompous account of a speaker staying calm while pursuing a realistic goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of speech' looks like part of the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is just 'theory' at the end, Marx's philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectical materialism is the Marxist philosophy of history and nature, a body of thought.

clue.text: Foreign ally questioning whether he can proceed?

wordplay.note: the asker's question, put in three short words, is whether he is cleared to go

explanation.surface: An ally from abroad asking whether he may go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM I GO, the answer asks whether one is cleared to proceed.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so an ally from a foreign tongue.

clue.text: Expel from school's front bench

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Kicking someone off the front bench at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expel' looks like school discipline; it means throw out.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to expel forcefully, pouring something out in a stream.

clue.text: Key expert's hint about wrong answer completely rejected

indicators.note: completely rejected means the whole construction is turned back to front
about means the hint word goes around the other pieces

explanation.surface: An expert's tip about a wrong answer is thrown out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. TIP around SIN and A gives TSINAIP, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is skilled at playing the keys of a piano, so an expert with keys.

clue.text: Moving to Fair Isle, fixing sort of gate with even more reason

indicators.note: fixing means setting firmly inside, so the gate goes into the mixed letters
moving means shifting about, so the letters of to fair are rearranged

parts.note: an OR gate is a type of logic gate

explanation.surface: Relocating to Fair Isle and repairing a gate there.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle, a Shetland island famous for knitwear, is split: its first word joins the anagram and 'Isle' gives its abbreviation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is a Latin phrase for an argument that holds all the more strongly.

clue.text: In Djibouti, putting away every second mug

indicators.note: taking out every second letter leaves the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Someone in Djibouti downing a drink every other moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup being put away; it means a dupe. Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is British slang for a gullible fool, so an idiot.

clue.text: Shyster, one who gives you a hand on horse

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the dealer comes after the horse

parts.note: a wheeler is the horse harnessed nearest the wheels

parts.words: one who gives you a hand
parts.note: the card dealer deals you a hand

explanation.surface: A crook who helps you up onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives you a hand' looks like helping; it is dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeler-dealer is a shrewd, scheming operator in business, close to a shyster or swindler.

clue.text: Drink with students, going over grim experience

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Having a drink with students over a miserable time.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK student body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, an evening drink.
